Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 2014-038 on Protection of Personal Data adopted December 2014, promulgated January 2015. Application not yet effective as no implementing decree published. Madagascar also ratified the Malabo Convention in June 2024. CMIL established December 2023 but not yet fully operational.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the DLA Piper source (last modified 4 February 2025), which confirms Law No. 2014-038 on the Protection of Personal Data was adopted 16 December 2014, promulgated 9 January 2015 and published in the Official Gazette 9 June 2015 — it 'has been in force for nine years'. The Comments already stated this but the Value Code was set to 1 (No), which does not match: the legislation demonstrably exists and is in force, even though full application awaits an implementing decree (a matter of enforcement/effectiveness, not existence). Revised from 1 to 2 (Yes) on the strength of this authoritative, directly-read source. Second originally cited source (caseguard.com) not re-verified as it was not needed to confirm the law's existence.
revised_comments: Madagascar's Law No. 2014-038 on the Protection of Personal Data, adopted in December 2014 and promulgated in January 2015, provides the country's data protection legal framework and covers personal data processed within the identity system. The law has been in force since 2015, although its full application awaits publication of an implementing decree. Madagascar also ratified the African Union's Malabo Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection in June 2024.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: CMIL (Commission Malagasy sur l'Informatique et des Libertés) established by Decree No. 2023-1541 dated 6 December 2023. Partially constituted but not fully operational as of 2025 (some member appointments pending).
revision_notes: Original DLA Piper source (fetched, last modified 4 February 2025) described the CMIL as established by Decree No. 2023-1541 (6 December 2023) but 'not fully operational' pending remaining member appointments, supporting the original Value Code of 1. However, fresher reporting found and fetched shows this has since changed: all CMIL members were formally appointed and took their oath of office on 5 August 2025 (Council of Ministers decree on nominations), reported by Midi Madagasikara/AllAfrica (6 August 2025) and Newsmada (5 August 2025), and the operationalisation was welcomed by the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie. The DPA is therefore now constituted and operational. Revised from 1 (No) to 2 (Yes) on the strength of these directly-read, dated news sources corroborating the government decree.
revised_comments: Madagascar's data protection authority, the Commission Malagasy sur l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL), is operational. Established by Decree No. 2023-1541 of 6 December 2023, the CMIL's full complement of members — representing the National Assembly, Senate, judiciary, private sector and technical/civil society bodies — was formally appointed and sworn in on 5 August 2025. The CMIL now exercises regulatory oversight of personal data collection, processing and sharing in Madagascar, including data linked to the identity system.
